messages.content:
You are a C test designer. Design high-level test scenarios (WHAT to test), not C code (HOW).

ROLE: Phase 1 of dual-phase architecture
- You: Design test for ONE execution path
- Phase 2: Converts your design to C code

INPUTS PROVIDED:
- Function signature, description, implementation (source code)
- ONE target execution path with conditions
- Operation map (available helper functions)

YOUR TASKS:
1. Analyze path: What conditions trigger it? What inputs? Expected behavior?
2. Study implementation: Understand branches, variables, edge cases for this path
3. Design test: Choose inputs that trigger path conditions (boundary, normal, edge, error cases)
4. Specify helpers: Assertions, utilities, dependencies from operation map
5. Define expectations: Return values, side effects, state changes, invariants
6. Provide rationale: Why this test matters, what bugs it catches

NO MOCKING ALLOWED:
Do NOT design tests requiring: mock functions, forced failures, simulated allocation failures, faked system calls.
ONLY use: Real inputs, natural error conditions (NULL, invalid params), actual boundary values.

Example - WRONG: "Test malloc failure handling" (requires mock_malloc_fail)
Example - RIGHT: "Test NULL pointer handling" (pass NULL directly)

SUCCESS CRITERIA:
✓ Test exercises the target path with correct inputs
✓ All assertions, helpers, dependencies specified
✓ Rationale clear and convincing
✓ Memory management specified (setup/cleanup)
✓ Valid JSON output with all required fields
✓ Test naming: test_<function>_<path_scenario>

OUTPUT: JSON object with metadata, test_scenarios array (1 scenario for the path), test_suite_summary.

test_metadata.description: Verify buffer_new_with_copy correctly allocates and copies a typical string into a new buffer.
test_metadata.rationale: This test ensures the main path (allocation succeeds) works for a normal, non-empty string, verifying correct memory allocation, data copying, and buffer invariants.

path_conditions: str is a valid, non-NULL pointer to a null-terminated string
expected_branches: memcpy copies len bytes from str to self->alloc

dependencies.name: buffer_new_with_size
dependencies.reason: Allocates buffer of required size for copy

assertions.name: helper_assert_buffer_content
assertions.purpose: Verify buffer's content matches the input string (excluding null terminator).
assertions.usage: Check that buffer->data matches the copied string.

assertions.name: helper_assert_buffer_length
assertions.purpose: Verify buffer's string length matches input string length.
assertions.usage: Check that buffer length equals strlen(input).

utilities.name: helper_cleanup_buffer
utilities.purpose: Free the memory allocated for the buffer.

preconditions: input_str is a valid, null-terminated, non-empty string
setup_requirements.initial_state: No buffer allocated; input string is valid and available.

primary_function_args.rationale: Covers the normal use case for copying a string into a buffer.

return_value.description: Pointer to a newly allocated buffer containing a copy of the input string (without null terminator).
return_value.validation: Returned pointer is non-NULL and buffer content matches input string up to strlen(str).

side_effects.effect: A new buffer is allocated and initialized with the copied string data.
side_effects.observable_via: Returned buffer pointer is non-NULL; buffer content matches input string.

state_changes: No buffer → New buffer allocated and initialized with input string
invariants_maintained: Buffer content matches input string (excluding null terminator)

assertions_required.description: Verify that buffer_new_with_copy returns a valid buffer pointer.
assertions_required.failure_meaning: Buffer allocation or copy failed unexpectedly.

assertions_required.description: Verify that the buffer's content matches the input string (excluding null terminator).
assertions_required.failure_meaning: Buffer did not copy the string correctly.

assertions_required.description: Verify that the buffer's length matches the input string length.

cleanup_requirements.final_state: All allocated memory is freed; no resource leaks.

operation_sequence: Call buffer_new_with_copy(input_str) and store result in buf
Assert buf->data matches "hello world" (excluding null terminator)
edge_cases_to_note: Input string must not be NULL (not tested here)
Input string is non-empty; empty string and very long string are other cases

path_coverage_analysis.description: Normal path: input string is valid, allocation succeeds, buffer is created and filled with copy.

integration_test_suggestions: Test with very long string input.
Test with input containing special characters or binary data.
